title: Keerthy Suresh Brings Contemporary Kanjivaram to TIFF 2026 Dorothy Premiere
excerpt: The actor walked the Toronto red carpet in a burgundy-and-gold Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble for the world premiere of her Tamil drama Dorothy, which earned a standing ovation in the festival's Centrepiece section.
body:
• Keerthy Suresh attended the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival for the world premiere of her Tamil film Dorothy, directed by Karthik Subbaraj.
  • She wore a burgundy and antique-gold contemporary Kanjivaram-inspired ensemble designed by Karan Torani and styled by Ami Patel, finished with traditional Kerala gold jewellery.
  • Dorothy premiered in TIFF's Centrepiece section to a standing ovation and is the first Tamil feature to screen at the festival in a decade.
  • The film, presented by Jio Studios with music by Ilaiyaraaja, opens in cinemas worldwide on September 25, 2026.

Keerthy Suresh carried South Indian textile heritage onto one of the world's most prominent red carpets on Friday, attending the world premiere of her Tamil film Dorothy at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. The actor walked the premiere at the Scotiabank Theatre in a contemporary ensemble inspired by the Kanjivaram silk saree, as the film screened to a standing ovation in the festival's Centrepiece section.

Suresh attended the premiere alongside director Karthik Subbaraj, co-stars Sananth and Rishikanth, and producers Guneet Monga Kapoor and Achin Jain of Sikhya Entertainment, according to reports from the festival.

The look: Kanjivaram, restructured

For the premiere, Suresh chose a custom outfit by designer Karan Torani, styled by Ami Patel, that reworked the visual language of the Kanjivaram saree into a structured contemporary silhouette. The burgundy and antique-gold ensemble featured a textured cropped blouse in a muted gold-brown shade, paired with a voluminous maroon skirt inspired by the Kanjivaram drape. The skirt carried a broad metallic-gold hem with subtle green detailing.

A brocade-style dupatta with gold motifs and an ornate border was draped around her shoulders and across the front, pulling the elements together. Suresh finished the look with layered Kerala gold jewellery, including necklaces with a dark black teardrop-shaped pendant at the centre and traditional gold drop earrings, with her hair styled into a sleek bun.

The styling choice fits a pattern Suresh has built across her public appearances: weaving Indian craft into modern silhouettes. Critics of the look were divided — one fashion columnist argued she would have preferred the Kanjivaram worn as a traditional drape — but the ensemble drew wide attention as one of the premiere's standout red-carpet moments.

Dorothy's festival moment

The premiere itself marked a milestone for Tamil cinema. Dorothy is the first Tamil feature to premiere at TIFF in a decade, placing Subbaraj's story before an international festival audience. The screening at the Scotiabank Theatre was met with a standing ovation, according to Filmfare, which reported from the festival.

Written and directed by Subbaraj, Dorothy stars Suresh alongside Sananth and Rishikanth in a story the filmmaker describes as rooted in a culture he knows intimately. Presented by Jio Studios and produced by Jyoti Deshpande, Guneet Monga Kapoor and Achin Jain in association with Dhammam Films, the film explores themes of friendship, identity, prejudice and human dignity.

"At its heart, Dorothy is a deeply human story about identity, belonging and the courage to find your way back to yourself."

— Guneet Monga Kapoor, Producer, Sikhya Entertainment

Monga Kapoor's own association with TIFF stretches back more than 15 years, through films including The Lunchbox, Gangs of Wasseypur and Kill. "TIFF has been an important part of Sikhya's journey," she and Achin Jain said in a statement, "and bringing Dorothy here feels particularly special."

The Ilaiyaraaja factor

The film's music has been a significant part of its pre-release attention. Dorothy is an Ilaiyaraaja musical, with the legendary composer providing the original score and songs. Two tracks, "Kalyana Virundhu" and "Muthumani," have each crossed 10 million views on YouTube, and both have featured among the top five trending music videos on YouTube India.

The music was also taken beyond the film through the Dorothy Concert in Chennai, where musicians performed the film's 18-track score continuously for around 40 minutes at the Image Auditorium, according to Bollywood Hungama.

A diaspora spotlight in Toronto

Toronto is home to one of North America's largest South Asian communities, and a Tamil-language premiere in the festival's Centrepiece section gives diaspora audiences an early encounter with a film before its theatrical run. For the diaspora, the moment sits alongside a broader wave of South Asian titles finding mainstream festival platforms — with Dorothy carrying the added weight of representing Tamil cinema at TIFF after a ten-year gap.

What's next

Following its festival premiere, Dorothy arrives in cinemas worldwide on September 25, 2026. The festival reception, combined with the momentum of its soundtrack, sets up the film's international rollout — and puts Suresh's TIFF appearance, and the Kanjivaram it celebrated, in front of a global audience.
